summary: Iosco County, MI tower in the Huron National Forest, completed by August 1935. Its top section is on display at a marker at Higgins Lake; the Hale site today is not described.

facts.design: standard stairway-type tower, 100 feet (30 m) from ground to cab peak
facts.status_note: Only the top part is on display, at Higgins Lake in Roscommon County, not at the Hale site.

events.note: Completed by August 1935 per an Ironwood Times item quoted by Forest Lookouts; the item places it in Iosco County south of Hale and east of West Branch

evidence.quote: Michigan's newest fire tower has just been completed.

evidence.supports: standard stairway type, 100 feet to cab peak, located south of Hale
evidence.quote: It is of the standard stairway type, 100 feet high from ground to peak of cabin and is located in Iosco county south of Hale and east of West Branch.

evidence.supports: new tower brought manned Michigan towers to 138
evidence.quote: Completion of the new tower brings the number of Michigan towers, now manned, to 138.

evidence.supports: top part of the Hale tower is displayed
evidence.quote: This is just the top part of the fire tower from Hale, Michigan.

evidence.supports: marker and display at Higgins Lake, Roscommon County
evidence.quote: Marker is in Higgins Lake, Michigan, in Roscommon County.

evidence.supports: marker erected by Michigan History Center and DNR
evidence.quote: Erected by Michigan History Center and Department of Natural Resources.

evidence.supports: marker reached from North Higgins Lake Drive
evidence.quote: It can be reached from North Higgins Lake Drive near Conservation Drive.

evidence.supports: photo taken January 2, 2023, listed with the marker, shows the top portion of one of the 154 towers
evidence.quote: The top portion of one of the 154 fire towers that were built.

sources.title: The Hale Fire Tower Historical Marker

notes_for_editor: The 1935 item is quoted by Forest Lookouts and names only a place south of Hale; the link to the Hale name is the page's. Status 'partial' rests on the marker text ('just the top part'); the marker's date and the date and manner of the move were not found, so no relocated event is recorded. HMDB is a user-submitted database, but the marker text is official ('Erected by Michigan History Center and Department of Natural Resources'). The 100 ft figure runs to the cab peak, so height_m was not entered; a human could decide whether to record about 30 m. No source describes the Hale site or its access today.
